recorded_lines: | Speech actuator, lowest latency | **pbshift** | MIT | C++17, pitch-synchronous voice path, 0.25–4×, automatable rate, Live tier 56–64 ms at 48 kHz (vendor) | Pre-1.0, 2 GitHub stars, self-reported metrics; not independently tested |

**pbshift.** MIT, C++17 static library, streaming pull API (`feed` → `available` → `read`), independent pitch/stretch, rate automatable between `feed()` calls, 0.25–4× (clamped), formant preservation, deterministic output. Its `Voice` path is pitch-synchronous and time-domain, which is the right family for speech; the vendor reports **56 ms (formant) / 64 ms (no formant)** Live latency at 48 kHz, versus ~99–128 ms for Studio-RT. The project is pre-1.0 and effectively unproven, so treat it as a **P0 challenger**, not a dependency to ship without measurement. It vendors a modified Signalsmith Stretch 1.3.2 for its extreme-speech path (MIT) and pffft (BSD-like).
